subject: SDK onramp & environment checklist — next steps and tech clarifications
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: SDK onramp & environment checklist — next steps and tech clarifications

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (from today’s discovery)
- Primary workload: product search + FAQ chat across web + mobile, expect ~200 rps peak, 30k unique queries/day.
- Security requirements: VPC egress, SSO (OKTA), audit logs retention 3 years, SOC2 evidence needed.
- Priority features: embeddings for semantic search, a lightweight reranker, structured output with tool-calling for inventory lookups.

Immediate next steps (what I’ll do)
1) Share a targeted SDK quickstart (Python + TypeScript) that shows auth, routing, and a simple tool-calling example. Attached: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf.
2) Provide a small sample repo (local-first) you can run to validate VPC egress and API key/SAML flows. Link to repo + a zipped sample attached.
3) Loop in Stephanie (solutions) and Karthik (platform) for a short technical deep dive to review network/firewall requirements and reranker configuration.

Questions for your team (what we need from you)
- Can you confirm whether the initial pilot runs inside your VPC or from a cloud-hosted integration environment? If VPC, we’ll need egress IPs to allow during testing.
- Do you have a preferred SSO integration owner we should include on the follow-up call?
- Any constraints on language preference? We’ll provide parity for Python and TypeScript samples.

Proposed schedule
- 1 week: tailored quickstart + repo (we’ll send by Thu EOD PST).
- 1 week after that: 60-min tech deep-dive (Stephanie/Karthik + your engs).

If that sounds good I’ll send the quickstart and propose times for the deep-dive.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this pilot forward.

– Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (6 pages)

Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SDK onramp & environment checklist — next steps and tech clarifications

Thanks Marcus — helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side before the deep-dive: 

1) Auth/SSO: We use OKTA and would prefer an SAML/OIDC flow for short-lived credentials. Can your SDK show an example of exchanging a SAML assertion or integrating with an existing OIDC provider?

2) VPC details: Pilot will run in our AWS account behind a NAT gateway. We can provide a small allowlist for egress IPs — please send what you need.

3) Embeddings/reranker: We want a simple architecture that uses embeddings for initial recall (FAISS) and then a reranker (lightweight LM-based) to re-order top-50. Is there an example of a reranker pipeline in TypeScript? We’d like both Python and TS, but TS is preferred for our frontend engineering team.

4) Tool-calling / structured output: we’d like to see a TypeScript sample that demonstrates a model returning structured JSON for an inventory lookup and then triggering a server-side tool (e.g., a fulfillment check).

Marissa — can you help with any pre-read on the SSO options?

Happy to meet Thu or Fri next week for the technical deep-dive (10–11am PST works on our end).

Best,
Sara
Sara Hayes
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Retail

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hayes <sara.hayes@acmeretail.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SDK onramp & environment checklist — next steps and tech clarifications

Hi Sara — thanks for the detail, this is great. Quick answers and pointers below; I’ll bring runnable examples to the deep-dive.

Auth / SSO
- We support API keys, short-lived tokens via OIDC, and SAML-backed provisioning. For OIDC we typically show a three-legged flow where your IdP issues a short-lived access token that the SDK exchanges for a session token.
- Example: TypeScript snippet for token exchange (paste below). We’ll include a complete Okta OIDC example in the repo.

TypeScript token exchange (example)
const exchangeToken = async (idToken) => {
  const resp = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/session/exchange', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ id_token: idToken })
  });
  return resp.json();
};

Embeddings + reranker pattern
- Suggested flow: 1) generate embeddings (512 dim) for corpus -> index in FAISS; 2) recall top-200, dense-score with model A; 3) rerank top-50 with model B configured for pairwise scoring.
- We include a TS sample that demonstrates calling embeddings endpoint + a reranker call (server-side). Reranker config is simple JSON: model, max_tokens, scoring_mode. We’ll include defaults tuned for latency/cost.

Structured output / tool-calling
- SDK supports structured JSON output via response schemas and a lightweight tool-calling hook. Example: the model returns {"sku": "1234", "available": true, "closest_store": "San Jose"} and the SDK triggers your fulfillment-check endpoint with that payload. We’ll provide an end-to-end sample app (TS) showing local mocking of the fulfillment tool.

Local testing & VPC egress
- The sample repo includes a docker-compose profile to run the quickstart locally and exercise connectivity from an ephemeral container.
- For VPC allowlisting: provide your egress NAT IPs and we’ll confirm the specific IP ranges/ports needed (HTTPS outbound to api.redwood.ai and optional metric endpoints).

Repo / links / attachments
- Public sample repo (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples (we’ll provide a branch with Acme-tailored examples).
- Attached to this thread: sample-repo.zip (TS + Python quickstart, docker-compose, reranker example).

I’ll bring a runnable demo of the TS tool-calling flow to the call and we can walk through SSO integration specifics.

— Stephanie
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
